transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump has wrapped his visit to China, where he held trilateral talks with Chinese
President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
As NPR's Charles Maynes reports, the visit was long on symbolism, but short on substance.
"Putin first raised the prospect of a trilateral meeting with Xi in a phone call with Trump
last October, and for the Russian leader, Trump's arrival was a win out of the gate,
the latest sign that Putin has effectively chipped away at Western attempts to isolate
him over his invasion of Ukraine."
President Xi also reveled in hosting the summit as proof of China's growing global clout.
And for Trump, the image of him warmly greeting U.S. geopolitical rival showed his norm-busting
style of foreign policy remains, even as he prepares for a democratic-led Congress at
home.
Yet the China summit resulted in little that was concrete.
The leaders issued a high-minded declaration of peace, but made no progress towards ending
their own wars in Ukraine and Iran.
Charles Maynes in PR News, Moscow.
"AI company Anthropik opened for trading in the biggest public stock offering ever today.
The debut happened despite investor fears of a possible A.I. bubble and public anxiety
that the technology threatens lives and livelihoods.
CEO Dario Amadei says the company is obsessed with safety and won't bend to business or
political influence."
"Today puts the company in a stronger financial position and in doing so only strengthens
our resolve to do the right thing.
If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an
incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same.
We call this a race to the top."
Anthropik's shares shot higher as trading began, closing up 17 percent.
Aid groups have published a 31-page report on President Trump's Gaza peace plan and PR's
Ayaba Traumi says the report found failings in how well the ceasefire is holding and access
to humanitarian aid.
The report by nine aid groups gave a failing grade to the implementation of the past year
of ceasefire in Gaza.
It noted Israeli attacks have killed more than 1,650 Palestinians during the ceasefire
and that Israeli forces have expanded their occupation of Gaza's territory.
The report said just 49 UN-coordinated trucks carried aid into Gaza in September, with only
2 percent carrying medical supplies.
Israel says Hamas is the main obstacle to improving conditions in Gaza and that it's
facilitating aid as needed.
The report by aid groups that include Oxfam and Refugees International says countries
should replace the Israeli approval process and military inspections of aid convoys with
an independent, transparent system.
Ayaba Traumi and PR News, Dubai.
Storms have brought record rains to South Florida, shifting north to the space coast
today.
Corners have overflowed, prompting water rescues for people and horses.
This is supposed to be Florida's dry season.
Nearly 17 inches of rain fell in 48 hours in Fort Lauderdale.
Meanwhile in California, rain continues to pound the coast, causing flash floods and
mudslides.
This is NPR News.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is meeting EU officials tomorrow to discuss closer ties
with the bloc that left in 2020.
Burnham wants to undo what he says is the damage caused by Brexit, and has suggested
that rejoining the EU is a future possibility.
It's a shift from the previous silence of British governments on reversing Brexit.
Singaporean entrepreneur Jack Sim invented World Toilet Day 25 years ago today.
NPR's Mark Silver reports it was inspired by the country's prime minister's comment
about the importance of clean toilets.
Sim wanted a day to devote attention to the fact that billions of people around the world
cannot find a safe and sanitary toilet.
It was adopted by the UN as an official day in 2013.
This year's theme is sanitation and gender equality.
Girls and women who don't have a toilet at home may venture out in unsafe areas that
makes them vulnerable to attack or harassment.
If their school or office does not offer sanitary facilities, they may opt to stay home during
menstruation.
Despite all the serious issues around toilets, it's okay to be joyful on World Toilet Day,
as Kate Olive-Medlakat with the World Health Organization.
World Toilet Day is my favorite day of the year.
It's really important, and it's an opportunity for us to celebrate and act on something that
many of us take for granted.
Four in ten people still do not have access to safe and sanitary toilets.
Mark Silver, NPR News.
A vibrant landscape painted by Vincent van Gogh weeks before his death has sold for $190.4
million at auction, the sale of Chateau in Fleur took place after an agreement between
its current owners and a Jewish family that sold it in Nazi-era Germany.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump wraps China visit with Xi and Putin talks, producing symbolism but no concrete progress
Anthropic opens for trading in largest public stock offering ever, closing up 17 percent
Aid groups' 31-page report gives failing grade to Trump's Gaza ceasefire and aid access
Record rains flood South Florida, with Fort Lauderdale receiving nearly 17 inches in 48 hours
Flash floods and mudslides hit California coast as rain continues to pound the region
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham meets EU officials on closer ties, suggests possible rejoining
Singaporean entrepreneur Jack Sim marks 25 years since inventing World Toilet Day
Van Gogh painting Chateau in Fleur sells for $190.4 million at auction after Nazi-era restitution deal
